latest_2026-05-22.condition_stage: Active Exudative Age-related Macular Degeneration (Wet AMD)
latest_2026-05-22.drafted_summary: The OCT scan of the left eye (OS) for patient P-2605-016, aged 65, reveals significant findings consistent with active exudative age-related macular degeneration (AMD). There is a substantial presence of subretinal fluid (SRF) and intraretinal fluid (IRF), indicating active leakage and exudation. Drusen are also noted, consistent with underlying AMD pathology. Critically, there is extensive disruption of the photoreceptor inner segment/outer segment (IS/OS) junction, suggesting significant damage to the photoreceptor layer. No subretinal hemorrhage (SHRM) was detected. These findings collectively point to an active and vision-threatening process.
latest_2026-05-22.suggested_action: Immediate ophthalmological consultation and initiation of anti-VEGF therapy are strongly recommended to address the active exudative process, reduce fluid accumulation, and prevent further vision loss. Close monitoring of treatment response with serial OCT scans is crucial. Further evaluation for potential choroidal neovascularization (CNV) with angiography (e.g., FFA/ICG) may be warranted if not already performed.
